verdict.rationale: Inngest has a first-party versioning doc saying developers can deploy function changes without explicit version markers or migration logic, and step memoization lets runs resume from checkpoints. The pack does not show how in-flight runs behave when code changes, whether they finish on their original version or get memoized steps reconciled against new code. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that in-flight runs complete on the version they started, details on handling step changes and determinism across deploys, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I deploy new workflow code while in-flight runs finish on the version they started with — versioning without breaking determinism

citations.quote: Inngest enables developers to deploy changes to functions without explicit version markers or complex migration logic.

Put side effects, API calls, sleeps, waits, and function invocations in steps so Inngest can memoize results, retry failures independently, and resume long-running work from the last successful checkpoint.
